chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibrahim al-Kazzaz, Abu Ayyub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who fainted for some days and did not pray, then regained consciousness. I asked: Does he pray what was missed? He said: 'There is no obligation upon him.'
ai.seo_question: Do I need to make up missed prayers if I was unconscious or fainting?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that prolonged unconsciousness (*ghafla*) serves as a complete exemption from the obligation of making up missed prayers (*qada*), distinguishing it from mere sleep or forgetfulness. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the *taklif* (religious burden) is suspended during periods where one lacks mental capacity or control, reflecting the divine mercy in easing obligations during states of incapacitation.
